segments.title: Chương 6: 0006 【Át bích. Bỏ qua】
segments.content:
The next morning was the comprehensive liberal arts exam.

Chen Guiliang thought he wouldn't know how to do it, but after getting the test paper, he found the first few questions were surprisingly simple.

But as he continued, he started to feel unsure about some questions.

They were clearly multiple-choice questions, yet there seemed to be several correct options.

He reviewed the questions repeatedly until his head went numb.

After haphazardly finishing all the questions, Chen Guiliang felt it wasn't too bad. Out of a total of 300 points for the liberal arts comprehensive, getting 160 should be no problem.

If he seriously reviewed this subject, it would be quite easy to raise his score.

Chen Guiliang turned in his paper early and returned to the dorm to continue writing his articles.

At lunch in the cafeteria, the woman serving food seemed to have a grudge against him. She didn't give him a single pleasant look and deliberately shook the ladle a few extra times.

With each shake, half the food disappeared.

It couldn't be helped. Back in high school, Chen Guiliang couldn't tolerate any injustice and liked to challenge everything and everyone.

Relying on the "no off-campus dining" rule, the school cafeteria had become more and more outrageous during his second year of high school. In the 40-degree summer heat, they didn't do anything with the leftovers and continued to sell them the next meal. The food was already spoiled, but they weren't the least bit afraid of sending students to the hospital.

Chen Guiliang had rallied several students to protest, even putting up a big-character poster on the principal's office door, and nearly got into a fight with the guards who were stopping students from going out.

Coupled with an incident where a student broke a bone climbing over the wall to eat out, the school was finally forced to lift the ban on off-campus dining.

As for the serving lady before him, she was also a piece of work.

Breakfast time was already tight, with a long line of students waiting for noodles. This lady saw the son of an acquaintance, not only did she let him cut to the very front of the line, but she also slowly ladled beef until the bowl was completely covered.

The bowl couldn't hold any more, yet she kept adding, finally piling the beef into a small mountain. Meanwhile, the other students' beef noodle soup had only a pathetic two small pieces of beef per bowl.

That bowl of noodles was so hot and full that it couldn't be carried away. The lady actually abandoned the queuing students and ran off to find a tray for her acquaintance's son.

Chen Guiliang had been starving at the time, and it was a rare occasion for him to have breakfast. He was so disgusted by the lady that he erupted on the spot.

Ultimately, it caused all the students in line to refuse to eat, and someone even smashed the cafeteria's bowls and dishes all over the floor.

But nothing happened to that lady. She was a relative of the cafeteria contractor.

Instead, Chen Guiliang, for leading the protest, was given a major demerit by the school!

"Not enough."

At this moment, Chen Guiliang pointed at his stainless steel tray, stubbornly standing at the food counter and refusing to leave.

The serving lady pretended not to hear and put down her ladle, motionless.

The students behind him grew more and more impatient. Some criticized Chen Guiliang for blocking the way, while others urged the serving lady to hurry up.

A lady from the next counter advised, "Just let it go."

It was unclear who she was advising.

The serving lady finally added half a ladle. Only after Chen Guiliang left satisfied did she curse under her breath, "That beggar, he'll starve to death one day!"

The lady next to her said, "Why are you picking a fight with him? He's already on probation."

"Someone like him should be expelled, he doesn't act like a student at all!" The serving lady didn't think she was at fault.

Chen Guiliang didn't know he had been cursed. He was hunched over the dining table, wolfing down his food. This young body of his seemed to be perpetually hungry.

After lunch, he continued to write.

The English exam started in the afternoon. Chen Guiliang felt pretty good about it, at least not the sense of helplessness he felt during the math exam.

"Great Hero Chen, let's go to the internet cafe!"

As he was leaving the exam hall, Xie Yang called out to him.

Chen Guiliang laughed, "I ate a lot today, so taking a one-jin shit will be a piece of cake."

Only then did Xie Yang remember the oath of "taking a one-jin shit for every internet session." He stood there with a pained expression for a long while before saying with immense frustration, "Forget it, forget it. I'll go after the Gaokao. My Magic 3 helmet is going to depreciate soon."

Then, the guy quickly went to eat and returned to the dorm to read novels.

People always need a trigger to grow.

The Xie Yang in Chen Guiliang's memory had barely managed to get into a second-tier university. He didn't know what had happened, but during his freshman year, Xie Yang suddenly matured.

He stopped playing games, stopped reading novels, and worked part-time while studying.

Xie Yang earned his own living expenses from his sophomore to senior years and even got into a 985 university for his master's degree. Later, he took the civil service exam and, through his own efforts and his brother's help, had been promoted to county magistrate by the age of 40.

That evening, Chen Guiliang finished writing the four articles.

The next day was a day off, making way for the junior students' midterm exams. The third-year teachers were busy grading papers.

Chen Guiliang walked for twenty minutes to the post office near the school.

He bought four envelopes, put the manuscripts and the submission guidelines inside, and sent them as registered mail to the Mengya editorial department. Actually, one envelope would have been enough, but he deliberately used multiple envelopes to increase the chances of his initial submissions passing review.

Then he went to the bank to check his account. He had 52.68 yuan left.

At this time, regardless of whether it was an inter-bank transaction, withdrawing money in a different city required a service fee, and the percentage charged was damn high.

But there were ways around it, such as both the depositor and withdrawer sharing one account.

That is, Chen Guiliang's parents would deposit money into the bank card in another city. Chen Guiliang could then use a secondary card or a passbook to withdraw the money from a related bank in the city where the account was opened, without paying a single cent in service fees.

Conversely, if Chen Guiliang deposited money into the account, his parents would have to pay a service fee to withdraw it in another city.

Pressing the withdrawal button on the ATM, Chen Guiliang took out 50 yuan.

This little bit of money on him wasn't enough to do anything. Chen Guiliang pondered how to earn some.

China at this time was full of business opportunities, but none of them had anything to do with a left-behind child. To make money, you either needed startup capital or connections.

Chen Guiliang had neither!

Write articles and submit them?

He could try, but it was too slow to make money, unless it became a bestseller after publication.

Chen Guiliang's mind was filled with wild thoughts as he muddled through the day off. He still had to attend evening self-study.

He went to the classroom with his roommates. It was bustling and noisy inside. But there were also many students who, oblivious to the noise, sat quietly at their desks, reading and practicing problems.

Chen Guiliang was in the liberal arts experimental class.

Although it was called an experimental class, some had gotten in through connections.

Chen Guiliang walked to the back row from memory. There were only three seats there, the thrones of the "Three Phantoms."

Besides Chen Guiliang, the other two of the "Three Phantoms" were both here because of connections.

There used to be the "Four Heavenly Kings," but one had transferred out in the third year of high school, returning to his so-called place of household registration. Heh, a Gaokao migrant.

"You're here?"

His deskmate, Guan Zhiqiang, shifted his butt a little, but his eyes remained glued to a novel.

Chen Guiliang smiled, "You're early."

Guan Zhiqiang's grades were at the bottom of the entire year. His looks were also hard to describe; at first glance, he looked rather dim-witted.

This fellow was always reading novels in class, giggling foolishly as he read, sometimes even drooling.

Chen Guiliang had always thought that the best Guan Zhiqiang could do was attend a vocational college.

He never would have expected that Guan Zhiqiang would suddenly become an art student and, unbeknownst to anyone, get into a certain academy of fine arts. After graduation, he stayed on at the school as a student counselor and later even became a leader in an administrative position at the art academy.

Having connections in the family really makes a difference. From high school to university to graduation, one can just coast along as a "connections case."

With Guan Zhiqiang's level of drawing skill, if you asked him to draw a turtle, it would come out looking like a crab. Who knew how he passed the art exam.

The last of the three phantoms in the class was that bastard, Li Jun.

Li Jun walked into the classroom with his hands in his pockets, a shiny MP3 player hanging around his neck. He strode to his seat with his head held high.

"Guan Zhiqiang!" Li Jun shouted loudly.

Guan Zhiqiang wiped the drool from the corner of his mouth and slowly turned his head to look over.

Li Jun showed off proudly, "I asked you to play mahjong, you son of a bitch, but you didn't come. I won over three hundred today."

"Heh heh," Guan Zhiqiang responded with a silly laugh.

He only looked stupid, he wasn't really stupid. He wasn't about to play mahjong with Li Jun. He had played a few times before, and Li Jun always ganged up with others to win his money.

Chen Guiliang couldn't be bothered with these two clowns. He was flipping through his math textbook.

He could understand some of the content, but some required reviewing first and second-year knowledge.

After an unknown amount of time, the classroom quickly quieted down.

The homeroom teacher, Liu Shuying, had arrived, with a tall girl following behind her.

As Chen Guiliang was familiarizing himself with the textbook, Guan Zhiqiang jabbed him in the arm, whispering excitedly like a pervert, "Look, look, a beauty!"

The entire class's attention was focused on the girl.

Especially the male students.

Guan Zhiqiang whispered, "Definitely the school beauty!"

Chen Guiliang glanced over and said nonchalantly, "A pair of Aces."

"What?" Guan Zhiqiang didn't understand.

Chen Guiliang added, "I pass."

The "pair of Aces" joke didn't exist yet, and with Guan Zhiqiang's touching IQ, it would probably be difficult for him to figure it out on his own.

The quiet classroom once again filled with murmurs, everyone secretly discussing the beauty.

"Clap, clap!"

The homeroom teacher, Liu Shuying, clapped her hands twice. "No more talking. We have a new student in our class. Let her introduce herself first."

The girl was probably about 1.7 meters tall, wearing a gray hoodie and blue jeans, looking fresh, casual, and sharp.

Her hair was tied in a single ponytail, with no other accessories.

Her eyebrows were a little thick, and her pair of phoenix eyes were bright and lively. She could be described as having thick brows and large eyes, which seemed to add a touch of heroic spirit to her entire person.

However, she was flat-chested.

An airfield.

She had a backpack slung over her left shoulder, her hands tucked into her hoodie pockets. She walked up to the podium and said in a Rongcheng accent, "My name is Bian Guanyue."

*No idea if Old Wang or Yue Guan won the bet, but in any case, the female lead is Yue Guan transformed, named Bian Guanyue.* Was the self-introduction over?

Liu Shuying was stunned for a moment, then said, "Very good, let's welcome student Bian Guanyue!"

The classroom erupted in thunderous applause. Guan Zhiqiang clapped particularly loudly, his mouth wide open, almost drooling.

Although they were all Sichuan dialects, the local dialect sounded too harsh.

Bian Guanyue, on the other hand, spoke with a provincial capital accent. Her plum blossom tone, delicate and soft, was like heavenly music to the ears of all the boys in the class.

So gentle.

The word "chuizi" (hammer) coming from such a girl's mouth would surely sound more pleasant than a local girl calling out "gege" (brother).

Xie Yang even had the thought of changing his affections. He repeatedly compared Zhou Jing and Bian Guanyue in his mind, and the more he compared, the more he felt Zhou Jing was crushed in every aspect.

Alas, student Zhou Jing, don't blame me for being a heartbreaker, it's just that the new student is too outstanding.

Xu Haibo had also been stealing glances, but he kept pretending to read a book. This kid would blush unconsciously just from saying a few extra words to a girl alone; how would he dare to look directly at a beauty like Bian Guanyue.

Li Jun suddenly stood up and waved, "Student Bian, I have an empty seat here, I have an empty seat here!"

He was the only one sitting alone in the whole class, with an empty desk beside him, left by the Gaokao migrant.

Bian Guanyue strode over and sat down next to Li Jun with a blank expression.

The boys were filled with envy.

That damn Li Jun is so lucky!

Li Jun tried to cozy up with a grin, "Student Bian, your name is really nice, just like a female warrior from a costume drama."

"Thanks," Bian Guanyue replied coldly.

Li Jun added, "My name is Li Jun. The Li from 'mu zi Li,' the Jun from 'junzi'."

Bian Guanyue did not respond.

"Clap, clap!"

Liu Shuying clapped her hands again. "Quiet! The midterm exam results are out. Some students have made great progress, while others, I don't know what they've been doing..."

Li Jun, who had been extremely excited, heard that the exam results were out and instantly shut his mouth.
